name: pile of broken concrete and brick rubble with rebar sticking out, lying on the ground
label: wasteland_ruins/rubble-pile

surfaces.part: rebar rods sticking out of the top

answer.evidence: The object is a single irregular dome-shaped heap. The silhouette widens steadily from 4 px at row 9 to 31 px at rows 25-29, then closes at rows 30-31. The pixels are a mottled mix of grey and brick-red chunks with no horizontal banding. The column scans at x=9, 16 and 24 show no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no ellipse width profile. The only dark run in the middle is a single dark chunk. The rebar at rows 9-13 is a small protruding detail and counts as decor. The heap has no separable top plane and front face, so it reads as a lumpy mound seen from the front rather than a three-quarter box or a flat top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The rubble pile has stones shaded one by one: concrete chunks in about 4-5 grey steps, reddish brick fragments, and rusty rebar tips. Dark edge pixels are only 4% near-neutral, so the outline is a tinted dark tone of the neighbouring material rather than a black sticker line. Near-flat coverage is 0%, with no 5x5 flat fills, and the broken, chipped silhouette carries variation. It shows 12 visible tones per tile, above the hedge (9) and a little below the cheese stall (17) and well (20). That is appropriate for a small prop with a 12-colour palette, so density is only slightly lower than the best references. It is a bit less textured than the roofed well, but a careful artist would accept it next to the hedge and stall without it looking like a flat sticker.
